children.text: Śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ
Mithyāgrahaṇam
children.translated_text: The Misjudgment (<s>Mithyāgrahaṇa</s>)
Salutation to the blessed <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.

children.text: Caitramāsasya sāyaṃ samayaḥ.
children.translated_text: It was the evening hour of the month of <s>Caitra</s>.

children.text: Mohamayyā mājhagāvanāmani sthāne kasyacic chrīlasya gehe kanyāyā vivāhasya maṇḍapamaṇḍanādiprāthamikasaṃbhāro 'nuṣṭhīyate sma.
children.translated_text: At a place called <s>Mājhagāva</s> in <s>Mohamayya</s>, in the house of a certain wealthy man, the preliminary arrangements — the decoration of the wedding pavilion and so forth — for the marriage of a daughter were being carried out.

children.text: Kvacin maṅgalapāṭhakānāṃ purohitānāṃ madhuravacanaiḥ
kaṭhinamaṇikuṭṭimasya nikhananaracanena
children.translated_text: with the hammering and arranging of the hard jeweled floor,

children.text: kvacit karmakarāṇāṃ kalakalena
children.translated_text: at other places with the commotion of the laborers

children.text: saṃcarajjanacaraṇavikṣepaṇadhvaninā
children.translated_text: with the sound of the footsteps of people moving about

children.text: kṣubhitam iva bhavanam etad abhavat.
children.translated_text: the house seemed as if in tumult.
At some places, with the sweet utterances of the auspicious-reciting priests

children.text: Paredyur hi kenacid dhanāḍhyena saha vatsāyā udvāho niścita āsīt.
children.translated_text: For the next day, the marriage of the young woman with a certain wealthy man had been decided.

children.text: Seyaṃ viṃśativarṣīyā kṛśāṅgī hrasvākṛtiḥ parimitavāgapi madhurasvarā
gauravarṇāpi nātirūpavaiśiṣṭyasaṃpannā
children.translated_text: fair-complexioned yet not endowed with exceptional beauty

children.text: Amīnābhidhāpi Mīnākṣī saha sakhyā Saralābhidhayā saralasvabhāvayā gaganatalacaramārdhavartini bhagavati divasādhināyake rasālādivṛkṣabhūṣitāyāṃ vāṭikāyāṃ svapitur mandirapakṣadvārasamīpasthāyāṃ vijanakoṇe bakulataror ekasyādhaḥ saṃlāpaṃ kurvaty āsīt.
children.translated_text: <s>Amīnā</s> by name — though [her name meant] 'fish-eyed' (<s>Mīnākṣī</s>) — was engaged in conversation with her friend named <s>Saralā</s>, who was straightforward by nature, in a secluded corner of the garden adorned with mango and other trees, near the side entrance of her father's mansion, while the blessed lord of the day was traversing the last quarter of the sky.
She was twenty years old, slender-limbed, of short stature, sparing of speech yet sweet-voiced

children.text: Patatriṇāṃ kilakilaravo 'staṃ gataḥ.
children.translated_text: The chirping of the birds had subsided.

children.text: Ālolamālatīpuṣpasamūhād utpatyālikadambakāni tūṣṇīkāṃ bhejire.
children.translated_text: Swarms of bees, having risen from the clusters of swaying jasmine flowers, had fallen silent.

children.text: Saralā: Sakhi
vivāhamaṅgalavidhis te kasmin muhūrte niścito 'sti śvaḥ?
children.translated_text: at what auspicious hour is your wedding ceremony determined for tomorrow?
<s>Saralā</s>: Friend

children.text: Amīnā: Astaṅgamanasamaye bhagavataḥ savituḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Amīnā</s>: At the time of the setting of the blessed sun.

children.text: Saralā: (sopahāsam) Ayi sakhi
varam adṛṣṭvā tatpāṇigrahaṇaṃ kathaṃ nāma pratipadyate tvayā?
children.translated_text: how can you agree to take the hand of the bridegroom without even having seen him?
<s>Saralā</s>: (with a smile) O friend

children.text: Amīnā: Taddarśanena kim?
children.translated_text: <s>Amīnā</s>: What is the use of seeing him?

children.text: Bhāratavarṣe bhūyiṣṭhānāṃ kanyānāṃ varasya darśanāt prāg eva vivāho bhavati.
children.translated_text: In <s>Bhāratavarṣa</s> (India), the marriages of most girls take place even before seeing the bridegroom.

children.text: Anatikrāntaśaiśavāpi madīyāmbā vivāhāt pūrvaṃ me pitṛpādānāṃ darśanāmandānandam
ā
labdhvāpi saha tair vastum agamat.
children.translated_text: and yet went to live with him.
My own mother, though she had not yet passed childhood, before the marriage obtained no less than the full joy of seeing my father

children.text: Ahaṃ tu viṃśativarṣīyāsmi.
children.translated_text: I am twenty years old.

children.text: Mātāpitarāv avalambamānā tayor ājñāṃ śirasāṅgīkṛtya niḥśaṅkaṃ niścitavarasya pāṇigrahaṇaṃ mudā kariṣye.
children.translated_text: Depending on my parents, accepting their command upon my head, I shall joyfully and fearlessly take the hand of the chosen bridegroom.

children.text: Saralā: Paraṃ yadi kumāro vivāhāt prāk paricitaḥ syāt tadā nijabhāvisukhāprāptau pratītā bhavet kumārī.
children.translated_text: <s>Saralā</s>: But if the young man were known before the marriage, then the maiden would be confident of obtaining her own future happiness.

children.text: Ittham abhidhāya Saralā kiñcin natvā bhūtale vistāritabakulapuṣpanikarāt kānicid vicitya tadāmodam āsvādayat.
children.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Saralā</s> bent down slightly, picked out some flowers from the heap of <s>bakula</s> blossoms spread on the ground, and savored their fragrance.

children.text: Amīnā: Hum! Pāścātyadeśīyānām evānukūlā prītivivāhādikalpanā.
children.translated_text: <s>Amīnā</s>: Hmm! The notion of love-marriages and the like is suitable only for those of Western countries.

children.text: Kṛtapraṇayavivāhānām api vadhūvarāṇāṃ vyabhicāraparasparasvabhāvā saṅgatyādikāraṇebhyaḥ pāścātyadeśeṣu vivāhaviśleṣasya vṛttaparamparā kriyāsamabhihāreṇa śrūyate.
children.translated_text: Even among brides and grooms who have married by choice, the series of marriage dissolutions in Western countries is heard of constantly, arising from causes such as infidelity, incompatibility of temperament, and association [with others].

children.text: Param asmadīyadeśe viralaḥ khalu vyatikaras tādṛśaḥ.
children.translated_text: But in our country, such deviation is rare indeed.

children.text: Ity Amīnā svapitur asakṛd uktaṃ vākyam udīrya kasyacit praphullagulamohorākhyadrumaviśeṣasyādho marakatopalakalpitāsandīṃ prati sakhīm anayat.
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Amīnā</s>, uttering the words her father had often spoken, led her friend toward a bench fashioned like an emerald gem, beneath a certain tree of the species called <s>Gulamohara</s> (Gulmohar), which was in full bloom.

children.text: Amīnā: Sarale! Jānāsi tvaṃ yac chakuntalāduṣyantayor anurāgabaddhayor gāndharvavidhinā svairaṃ pariṇītayor api katipayakālottaraṃ vicchinnaprāyo 'bhūd vivāhaḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Amīnā</s>: <s>Saralā</s>! You know that even though <s>Śakuntalā</s> and <s>Duṣyanta</s>, bound by mutual love, were freely married by the <s>Gāndharva</s> rite, after some time their marriage was nearly severed.

children.text: Saralā: Paraṃ śāpaprabhāvāt kupitasya
Durvāsa
children.translated_text: <s>Durvāsas</s>

children.text: munes tat saṃvṛttaṃ na tu tayor doṣāt.
children.translated_text: , not through any fault of theirs.
<s>Saralā</s>: But that happened through the power of the curse of the enraged sage

children.text: Kumāryāv ime āśaiśavāt prativeśinyāv āstām.
children.translated_text: These two maidens had been neighbors since childhood.

children.text: Yady api bhinnabhinnarītyā saṃvārdhite adhyāpite bhinnabhinnaś ca tayor naikaviṣayeṣu gṛhasaṃskāro 'bhūd
bhinnabhinne ca dharmamate abhūtāṃ tayos tad apīme parasparaṃ pratibaddhadṛḍhasakhye ciraṃ sthitavatyau.
children.translated_text: and their religious convictions too were different, still, these two had long remained bound in firm mutual friendship.
Although they were raised and educated in different ways, and the domestic culture of each in many subjects was different

children.text: Amīnā hi kanyāśālāyām adhyāpitāpi svātantryasukhaṃ nānvabhavat.
children.translated_text: Although <s>Amīnā</s> had been educated in a girls' school, she had not experienced the happiness of independence.

children.text: Seyaṃ vyaktitvavihīnā bhāvanāvarjitā vaivāhikaviṣaye na kam api pakṣam avālambata.
children.translated_text: She, devoid of individuality, lacking in reflection, held no particular position on the subject of marriage.

children.text: Tasyā vivāhavāṅniścayo Hamidanāmnā kenacid dhanāḍhyena śilpayantrasvāminā saha pitṛbhyāṃ vyadhāyi.
children.translated_text: The promise of her marriage was arranged by her parents with a certain wealthy factory-owner named <s>Hāmid</s>.

children.text: So 'yaṃ taruṇo mohamayyāṃ eva kṛtavāso 'bhūt.
children.translated_text: This young man had been residing in <s>Mohamayya</s> itself.

children.text: Vastutaḥ pitur ājñayā kasyāpi kumārasya pāṇigrahaṇaṃ mugdheyam aṅgyakariṣyat.
children.translated_text: In truth, this simple girl would have accepted the hand of any young man by her father's command.

children.text: Atha paredyuḥ samāhitanānāvidhasaṃskāram Amīnāyāḥ pitur mandiraṃ mahotsavamayaṃ saṅgītanṛtyādidhvanimayaṃ divyamandiram iva vyabhāsiṣṭa.
children.translated_text: Then the next day, <s>Amīnā</s>'s father's mansion, adorned with various preparations, ablaze with the sounds of music, dance, and song, appeared like a celestial palace in the midst of a grand festival.

children.text: Krameṇa samupatiṣṭhadbhiḥ prāghuṇikaiḥ sadanam etad vyarājata.
children.translated_text: Gradually, as guests arrived, the house grew resplendent.

children.text: Āmadhyarātraṃ ca samucitabhojanaiḥ satkṛtaḥ prāghuṇikasamūho vārāṅganānṛtyasaṅgītādibhiḥ prāpitavinodaḥ śrīlasyālaye sukhaṃ kālam ayāpayat.
children.translated_text: Until midnight, the gathering of guests, honored with appropriate feasts and entertained by the dances and songs of courtesans, passed the time happily in the wealthy man's residence.

children.text: Nirvartitavivāhā prātastarāṃ ca vadhūr mṛgamadakarpūrādinā surabhidravyeṇānuliptasarvāṅgī dhautadukūlavasanā dhavalapuṣpamaṇḍitaśirā ratnakhacitakaṇṭhahārakuṇḍalakaṅkaṇābharaṇabhūṣitā patyur geham ayāt.
children.translated_text: Early in the morning, the bride, her marriage completed, her entire body anointed with fragrant substances like musk and camphor, dressed in washed silk garments, her head adorned with white flowers, bedecked with jewel-studded necklace, earrings, bangles, and ornaments, went to her husband's house.

children.text: Bālasakhīṃ Saralāṃ visraṣṭum asahamānā navoḍheyaṃ pitur gehān nigamanāt prāg yathā pratiśrutaṃ pratidinaṃ vāhakena sārdhaṃ premodrekasaṃbhṛtaṃ patraṃ prāhiṇot.
children.translated_text: Unable to bear parting from her childhood friend <s>Saralā</s>, this newly-wed bride, before departing from her father's house, sent a letter brimming with affection through a messenger every day, as she had promised.

children.text: Avarṇayac ca lekhe samudrataṭasthaṃ dīpamālāvihitabahulacākacakyaṃ hṛdayahāri saudhaṃ patyuḥ
samudbhāsamānaṃ saṃkhyātigāminā caturaviśiṣṭaveṣadhāriṇā paricchadena samanvitaṃ
children.translated_text: resplendent, furnished with an innumerable retinue wearing distinctive attire

children.text: nānāvidhapuṣpāmodasurabhitāntaḥpuraṃ
children.translated_text: the inner quarters fragrant with the scent of various flowers

children.text: nijāmūlyaratnakhacitābharaṇajātaṃ
children.translated_text: her own priceless collection of jewel-studded ornaments

children.text: payonidher madhuramarmarormimālā yās tasyā mārtaṇḍatāpaklāntiṃ mantharīkurvanti sma divā
children.translated_text: the rows of sweet murmuring waves of the ocean that would soothe her weariness from the sun's heat during the day

children.text: naktaṃ ca vījayantyo mandānilaṃ samacārayan.
children.translated_text: and at night, fanning with gentle breezes, would bring comfort.
She described in the letter the heart-captivating mansion of her husband, situated on the seashore, ablaze with the brilliance of many lamps

children.text: Yac cāsan Hāmidasya bhūyāṃsi yantravāhanāni
mandurā cānekavājibhiḥ saṃbhṛtā.
children.translated_text: and a stable furnished with many horses.
And that <s>Hāmid</s> had many motor vehicles

children.text: Iti sarvam eva savistaram Amīnayā sagauravaṃ varṇitaṃ
paraṃ svabhārtāram adhikṛtya leśamātram api na kadāpi śaṃsitam iti Saralayā lakṣitam.
children.translated_text: but <s>Saralā</s> noticed that not even the slightest mention was ever made about her own husband.
All this indeed was described in detail by <s>Amīnā</s> with pride

children.text: Na tu tayāpi Hāmidam uddiśya kim apy anuyuktam.
children.translated_text: Yet she too never asked anything regarding <s>Hāmid</s>.

children.text: Navoḍheyaṃ pitur gehaṃ bālasakhīṃ cānavarataṃ smāraṃ smāraṃ patyur adṛṣṭapūrve 'samāne prāsāde calantī mātṛvirahitāṃ naṣṭādhvakāṃ navaśukīṃ mahāraṇye
drumād
children.translated_text: from tree

children.text: drumam uḍḍayamānam ivātmānam akalayad Amīnā.
children.translated_text: to tree.

This newly-wed bride, constantly remembering her father's house and her childhood friend, moving about in her husband's unprecedented and unequaled palace, felt herself like a young parrot that had lost its way, separated from its mother, in a great forest, flying

children.text: Nirmito 'bhūd hi prāsādo 'yaṃ nānāmūlyadurlabhopalajātena.
children.translated_text: For this palace had been constructed from various costly and rare precious stones.

children.text: Aṃtarāṅgaṇe sugahanagṛhābhyantarmārgaparamparā marakatastambhāvalambitā sthitā.
children.translated_text: In the inner courtyard, a labyrinth of dense interior passages stood supported by emerald pillars.

children.text: Sukhopabhājāṃ mogaladharādhipānāṃ kālād avaśiṣṭāś citritāh paṭalā viśvakarmasamaśilpikarmakauśalabhūṣitā āsan.
children.translated_text: Painted canvases surviving from the era of the <s>Mogala</s> (Mughal) rulers, who had enjoyed prosperity, remained, adorned with craftsmanship equaling that of <s>Viśvakarman</s>.

children.text: Antaḥpurasya bhūtalaṃ cotkṛṣṭapārasīkadeśīyakauśeyāstaraṇair ācchāditam abhūt.
children.translated_text: The floor of the inner quarters was covered with exquisite Persian silk carpets.

children.text: Bhittayo 'pi kārmikakṣaumapaṭṭair āvṛttāḥ.
children.translated_text: The walls too were draped with linen tapestries.

children.text: Antaḥpurasya viśālāṅgaṇaṃ parilambamānarajatapañjarakrīḍākulaṃ śukasārikākulaṃ kalaravamanoharam.
children.translated_text: The spacious courtyard of the inner quarters was charming with the melodious sounds of parrots and <s>sārikā</s> birds playing about in hanging silver cages.

children.text: Pārśvavartiny ekasmin kāṣṭhajālālaye 'nye patatriṇo mayūrādayaḥ kujankalakalaiḥ pakṣasphuraṇaiḥ samañjīraśiñjananartanaiś cākrīḍan.
children.translated_text: In a nearby wooden aviary, other birds — peacocks and the like — sported with cooing and cackling, with fluttering of wings, and with dancing accompanied by the jingling of ankle-bells.

children.text: Vivāhāt pūrvaṃ mātugṛhe bhāvivivāhaviṣayaṃ vyacintayad Amīnā:
children.translated_text: <s>Amīnā</s> pondered about her forthcoming married life while still at her mother's house before the wedding:

children.text: Api madvivāhaḥ śrīleṇa saha Hāmidena sukhāvaho bhavitā.
children.translated_text: 'Will my marriage with the wealthy <s>Hāmid</s> be a source of happiness?'

children.text: Kathaṃ nāmaikākinī viśālasaudhe 'smin kālaṃ yāpayituṃ prabhaveyam iti.“
children.translated_text: 'How shall I be able to spend my time all alone in this vast mansion?'

children.text: Amīnā hy ādau vyavasāyābhāvāc chūnyahṛdayam ātmānam apaśyat.
children.translated_text: <s>Amīnā</s> at first, for lack of purpose, saw herself as empty-hearted.

children.text: Tadbhartā hi prātastarāṃ nagarāt sārdhayojanadūrasthaṃ śilpayantrakāryālayaṃ prati gṛhāt nirgatya sāyaṃ sūryāstamanasamaye nyavartata.
children.translated_text: For her husband would leave the house early in the morning for his factory-workshop, situated a league and a half from the city, and would return in the evening at sunset.

children.text: Athāvicchinnaviviktatāyāṃ saudhasya taruṇīyaṃ tāmbūlaṃ carvantī
dāsībhih pādayor nipīḍyamānā
children.translated_text: have her feet pressed by maidservants

children.text: vidyudvyajanena cakrākāreṇa vījyamānā svabhāgyodayasopānaṃ manasi praśaṃsantī
children.translated_text: be fanned by a circular electric fan, praising in her mind the stairway of her own good fortune

children.text: ajñabhṛtyetarajanasaṃparkarahitā
children.translated_text: without contact with any person other than ignorant servants

children.text: caturasakhīvirahitā
children.translated_text: bereft of the company of clever friends

children.text: vividhabhūṣaṇavihitaprabalacākacakyā
children.translated_text: dazzling with the brilliance of various ornaments

children.text: sugandhitailaprasādhitakeśakalāpā
children.translated_text: her tresses adorned with fragrant oil

children.text: añjanarañjitalocanāñcalā
children.translated_text: the corners of her eyes colored with collyrium

children.text: hiraṇmayasūtrāṅkitapaṭṭāmbaradharā
children.translated_text: wearing silk garments embroidered with golden threads

children.text: sāgarormimālātuṣārakaṇikāpaharaṇaśītasya samīrasya sukhasparśam anubhavantī
children.translated_text: experiencing the pleasant touch of the breeze, cool from carrying away the spray-drops of the ocean waves

children.text: śukasārikādipakṣiṇāṃ kalakalaṃ śṛṇvatī
children.translated_text: listening to the chattering of parrots, <s>sārikā</s> birds, and other birds

children.text: aṭṭālikāyā aṭṭālikām aṅganād aṅganaṃ paunaḥpunyena paryaṭantī kālam ayāpayad Amīnā yāvat prāsūta yamalau sutau.
children.translated_text: Wandering repeatedly from terrace to terrace, from courtyard to courtyard, <s>Amīnā</s> passed her time until she gave birth to twin sons.
And so, in the unbroken solitude of the mansion, this young woman would chew betel

children.text: Atha katipayavarṣottaraṃ tasyā bālasakhyāḥ saralāyāḥ kaścid viśvasanīya ṛjusvabhāvas taruṇaḥ pāṇim agṛḥnāt.
children.translated_text: Then, after some years, a certain trustworthy, straightforward young man took the hand [in marriage] of her childhood friend <s>Saralā</s>.

children.text: Tayoś ca vivāho vināḍambaraṃ niravartata.
children.translated_text: And their wedding took place without pomp.

children.text: Vyavasāya pravāsinaḥ Saralayāḥ patyur nāsīt sthiro nivāsaḥ kvāpi.
children.translated_text: <s>Saralā's</s> husband, being a traveling businessman, had no fixed residence anywhere.

children.text: Paraṃ svakāryārthaṃ mohamayīṃ gatāgataṃ kurvann eṣa nagarīm imām adhivastuṃ matiṃ kṛtvā Saralāyā icchām anusarann Amīnāyāḥ prasādasyādhastāt dvitraprakoṣṭātmakaṃ vasatisthānam alpiṣṭham upalabdhavān.
children.translated_text: However, coming and going to this enchanting city for his own business purposes, he decided to settle [here] and, following <s>Saralā's</s> wish, obtained a very small dwelling of two or three rooms beneath <s>Amīnā's</s> palace.

children.text: Ativiśālasaudhe 'smin naikabhāṭakabhavanayukte bahutithaṃ kālam uṣitvāpi tatra nivāsino 'nyonyadṛṣṭipatham api prāyo neyuḥ.
children.translated_text: In this extremely spacious mansion, which had many tenant apartments, even though they lived for a long time, the residents rarely even came within each other's line of sight.

children.text: Amīnāyā antaḥpuravalabhituṅgavātāyanād adho bhūtalasthasya Saralāyā gṛhasya sūkṣmakārpāsavastrācchāditavātāyanāntaḥprakoṣṭhaṃ sphuṭaṃ bahisto dṛkpatham agamat.
children.translated_text: From the high window of <s>Amīnā's</s> inner quarters, the inner room of <s>Saralā's</s> ground-floor house, covered with thin cotton curtains at the window, was clearly visible from outside.

children.text: Yadā ca Saralāyāḥ patir nagarān nirayāt tadā sā manaso dvitīyanibandhanabhūtayāḥ sadane 'mīnāyā bhūyiṣṭham aho 'nayat.
children.translated_text: And whenever <s>Saralā's</s> husband was away from the city, she spent most of her day at the home of <s>Amīnā</s>, who was the second anchor of her heart.

children.text: Ime ca sahacaryau punaḥ saṅgamenāmandānandam anvabhūtām.
children.translated_text: And these two companions experienced boundless joy at their reunion.

children.text: Athāminā svadharmaniyamam anusṛtyā'vaguṇṭhanapaddhatiṃ nibhṛtavāsaviśeṣāvasthitim aṅgīkṛtya kvacid eva vihārāya
gṛhād
children.translated_text: from the house

children.text: bahir niragāt.
children.translated_text: outside.
Now <s>Amīnā</s>, following the rules of her religion, accepting the practice of veiling and the condition of secluded living, only occasionally went out for recreation

children.text: Ato nāgarikāṇāṃ prativeśināṃ vā vṛttānabhijñāpi krameṇa saṃjātabahuprajā paraṃ saṃtuṣṭā
sta.

children.translated_text: Therefore, even without knowledge of the affairs of the townspeople or neighbors, she gradually became the mother of many children, and remained content

children.text: Yadā yadā tu Saralā nijasukhātiśayaḥ svabhartuḥ sāhacaryaṃ
tadviprayogottarapratyāgamanotkaṇṭhā cobhayor ity ādiviśayam adhikṛtya samalapat
children.translated_text: the longing for his return after their separation, and such topics

children.text: tadā tadāmīnāṃ vidūrabaddhadṛṣṭim alakṣayat sā.
children.translated_text: then each time, [<s>Saralā</s>] noticed <s>Amīnā</s> with her gaze fixed far away.
Whenever <s>Saralā</s>, whose own happiness was overflowing, would speak about the companionship of her own husband

children.text: Atha gacchati kale dṛṣṭyām Amīnayāḥ ko 'pi khedadyotako vikāro vyaloki.
children.translated_text: Then, as time passed, some change betraying sorrow was observed in <s>Amīnā's</s> expression.

children.text: Tayor nivāsayoḥ puraḥsthasya payonidhes taṭe saprema grathitānyonyakarau Saralāṃ tatpatiṃ ca rajanyāṃ śatapadīṃ kurvāṇā darśaṃ darśam Amīnāyāḥ viṣaṇṇatā vṛddhim agamat.
children.translated_text: On the shore of the ocean that lay before their dwellings, watching <s>Saralā</s> and her husband walking at night, their hands lovingly clasped together, <s>Amīnā's</s> despondency grew from sight to sight.

children.text: Sā ca dīrghaṃ niḥśvasatī durmanāyamāneva kvacid ātmānaṃ saroṣam aprākṣīt kuto niḥśvasyate mūḍhena tvayettham iti.
children.translated_text: And she, sighing deeply, becoming melancholy, sometimes angrily asked herself: 'Why do you, foolish one, sigh like this?'

children.text: Tāvan nikhile 'hani bhartur mukhadarśanānandaṃ kṣaṇikam evopalabdhavatī sā.
children.translated_text: Throughout the entire day, she experienced only a momentary joy at seeing her husband's face.

children.text: Sahanivāsināv api tāv adhikādhikam asaṃbaddhau sthitau.
children.translated_text: Though living together, the two [<s>Amīnā</s> and <s>Hāmid</s>] remained increasingly disconnected.

children.text: So 'yaṃ hi Hamido dyutapriyo naikakrīḍāmaṇḍaleṣu pratyahaṃ vinoditātmā gehaṃ nivartituṃ dine dine 'dhikādhikaṃ vyalambata.
children.translated_text: For this <s>Hāmid</s>, being fond of gambling, entertaining himself daily at various gaming circles, delayed returning home more and more each day.

children.text: Sā cādhīratayā patiṃ pratirātraṃ pratīkṣamāṇāsta.
children.translated_text: And she, with restless anxiety, sat waiting for her husband every night.

children.text: Paraṃ krameṇa yadā svapatyāgamasamaya āprabhātaṃ vilambitaḥ samabhūt tadā mā pratīkṣasva māṃ
bhojanaṃ samāpya yathākālaṃ svapihi.
children.translated_text: finish your meal and go to sleep at the proper time.
But gradually, when the time of his arrival was delayed until almost dawn, [he said:] 'Do not wait for me

children.text: Ahaṃ hi suhṛdbhiḥ sagdhiṃ kariṣya iti Hamidas tām ajñāpayat.
children.translated_text: For I shall dine with friends.' Thus <s>Hāmid</s> instructed her.

children.text: Sā ca tasya vilambasya kāraṇaṃ nitarāṃ jñātukāmāpi kutas tvayā'dya cirāyitam iti taṃ praṣṭum alaṃ dhairyaṃ na vā dṛḍhāgrahaṃ bheje.
children.translated_text: And she, though greatly desirous of knowing the reason for his delay, did not muster enough courage or firm resolve to ask him: 'Why have you been so late today?'

children.text: Evaṃ tayor vaivāhikasaṃbandhe kathāśeṣamātre saṃjāte hanta svapatiṃ sā nijasantater janaka ity evāvalokayamāsa.
children.translated_text: Thus, when their marital bond had become a mere remnant of a story — alas! — she regarded her own husband merely as the father of her children.

children.text: Prāyeṇa bhūyasīnāṃ dhīmatīnāṃ paristhityedṛkśocanīyayā bhāvyam iti manvānā patipremānandarase svapne 'py anāsvādite 'pi nijāvasthāṃ śocanīyāṃ nāmanyatāmīnā manāg api.
children.translated_text: Thinking that 'most intelligent women must face such a pitiable situation,' and never having tasted even in dreams the nectar of a husband's love, <s>Amīnā</s> did not consider her own condition to be pitiable in the slightest.

children.text: Athaikadeyaṃ payodhiphenapāṇḍure śayanīye kṛtapadā prasvāpasukham anubabhūva.
children.translated_text: Then one day, having placed her feet on a bed white as sea-foam, she enjoyed the pleasure of sleep.

children.text: Samayo 'yaṃ kila grīṣmartoḥ.
children.translated_text: This was the season of summer, indeed.

children.text: Avasare 'smin sarvato niśānāthasya saṃpūrṇakalāprāyasya dyutidugdhā dhavaladharā nicayena dhavalitam āsīd dharātalam.
children.translated_text: At this time, the earth was whitened by masses of white clouds washed with the radiance of the moon, who was nearly full in all his digits.

children.text: Jalanidher jalāni hīrakanicaya iva cākacakyaṃ bhejire.
children.translated_text: The waters of the ocean took on a glittering brilliance like heaps of diamonds.

children.text: Pihiteṣu bhavanadvāreṣu svasvaprakoṣṭheṣu parijanāḥ prasuptā āsan.
children.translated_text: With the doors of the buildings closed, the household members slept in their own rooms.

children.text: Amīnāpi prasvapatī kamapy atimātrāramyaṃ svapnam adrākṣīt.
children.translated_text: <s>Amīnā</s> too, while sleeping, saw some extraordinarily beautiful dream.

children.text: Yat tadīyabālasakhyā Saralayā tadīyasarvasvam api viluṇṭhya sā Hamidasya harmyān niṣkāsiteti.
children.translated_text: Namely, that her childhood friend <s>Saralā</s> had plundered all her possessions, and she had been expelled from <s>Hāmid's</s> mansion.

children.text: Caṇḍavātyayā sahasā prahateva sarutaṃ prabudhya śayanāt
samutthāya
children.translated_text: rose from the bed,

children.text: nayane parimṛjatī saṃbhrameṇa ruddhakaṇṭhā cakitacakiteva viśithilāṅgayaṣṭiḥ skhalatpādābhyāṃ samīpavartinaḥ saudhasyādho bhūtalasthaṃ Saralāyā nilayam avalokyantī vātāyanasamīpaṃ ciram avatasthe.
children.translated_text: rubbing her eyes, her throat constricted with agitation, startled and trembling, her body limp, with stumbling feet, stood for a long time near the window, looking down at <s>Saralā's</s> dwelling on the ground floor of the adjacent mansion.
As if suddenly struck by a whirlwind, crying out, she awoke from sleep,

children.text: Nitāntaviviktatayā viṣaṇṇamanā Amīnā jalābdher ūrmimālāyā mandamandamarmaraṃ śrāvaṃ śrāvaṃ parimṛditamṛṇālinīva mlānāṅgī priyajanasya kasyāpi mṛdulasparśajuṣaḥ sāntvanasyābhilāṣukābhūt.
children.translated_text: Utterly melancholy from the profound solitude, <s>Amīnā</s>, hearing again and again the gentle murmur of the ocean waves, like a crushed lotus plant, her body wilting, felt a longing for the soothing, tender touch of some dear person.

children.text: Tāvat Saralāyāḥ śayyāgāraṃ vidyuddīpakadyotitaṃ vyaloki tayā.
children.translated_text: Just then, <s>Saralā's</s> bedroom, illuminated by an electric lamp, was observed by her.

children.text: Vātāyanasya sūkṣmanepathyasya pṛṣṭhataḥ Saralāyāḥ sukumāraśarīrayaṣṭir itas tataś calantī dṛggocaratām agād Amīnayāḥ.
children.translated_text: Behind the thin curtain of the window, <s>Saralā's</s> delicate figure, moving here and there, came within <s>Amīnā's</s> sight.

children.text: Bhartari niryate nagarān niśīthinyāṃ kinnāma kartuṃ pravṛttā syāt Saraleti vyacintayat savismayam Amīnā.
children.translated_text: 'When her husband is away from the city, what on earth is <s>Saralā</s> doing in the middle of the night?' — <s>Amīnā</s> wondered with astonishment.

children.text: Atha yāvat sakhīṃ samāhvayituṃ pravartate sā tāvat tasyaiva saudhasyādho gṛhapṛṣṭhabhāgato nirgacchantīṃ Hamidasyākṛtim iva kasyāpi puruṣasyākṛtiṃ vyalokayad Amīnā.
children.translated_text: Then, just as she was about to call out to her friend, <s>Amīnā</s> observed from the rear portion of the house below that very mansion a figure of some man resembling <s>Hāmid's</s> form emerging.

children.text: Tadanu ca jhaṭiti Saralāyāḥ śayyāgṛhasya dipikā nirvāpitābhut.
children.translated_text: And then, instantly, the lamp in <s>Saralā's</s> bedroom was extinguished.

children.text: Nīravaṃ nibhṛtaṃ pracalan puruṣo 'yaṃ svapatir iti kṣaṇaṃ sā na vyaśvasīt paraṃ yadā svaharmyasya bahir dvāram udghāṭyāntaḥ sa prāviśat tadāyaṃ Hamidam antarā na
ko 'py
children.translated_text: than

children.text: anya iti pratītā'bhūt.
children.translated_text: <s>Hāmid</s>.

Moving silently and stealthily, this man was her own husband — for a moment she did not believe it, but when he opened the outer door of her own mansion and entered inside, she became convinced that this was none other

children.text: Pāṇḍuvadanā vepamānavigrahā kiṃkartavyapratipattimūḍhā sthitavatī ca.
children.translated_text: Pale-faced, her body trembling, bewildered about what to do, she stood still.

children.text: Prabhātaprāyaḥ samayo na cirād bhavitā.
children.translated_text: The time was nearly dawn, it would not be long.

children.text: Kuta etāvān vilambaḥ pratyāgamasya bhartuḥ
kutaś ca Saralāyāḥ śayanagṛhaṃ madhyarātre prakāśitaṃ syād ity anekavitarkajālenākrāntā vātāyanāt parāvṛtyonnidranetryābhānūdayaṃ saṃbhrāntā'ntaḥpure gatāgatam akarod Amīnā.
children.translated_text: and why would <s>Saralā's</s> bedroom be lit up at midnight? — caught in a web of many conjectures, turning away from the window, with sleepless eyes, anxious, <s>Amīnā</s> paced back and forth in the inner quarters until sunrise.
Why such a great delay in her husband's return

children.text: Paredyur niśīthe punar gavākṣasavidhe sā ciraṃ sthitvāpi Saralāyā nilayam andhatamasāvṛtam apaśyat.
children.translated_text: The following night, she again stood for a long time near the window, but saw <s>Saralā's</s> dwelling enveloped in utter darkness.

children.text: Bahiḥ sarvatra praśāntatādevī vyarājat.
children.translated_text: Outside, the goddess of tranquility reigned everywhere.

children.text: Yāminīkāminīvadanatilakabindur induś candrikāvyājenāmbaratalāt sudhādhārābhir dharātalam adhāvat.
children.translated_text: The moon — the tilaka-mark on the face of the beloved night — under the guise of moonlight, washed the earth's surface from the sky's dome with streams of nectar.

children.text: Antarāntarā vāridhivīcimālānāṃ mandamandaravo 'mīnāyāḥ karṇaśaṣkulīm apūrayat.
children.translated_text: Intermittently, the gentle murmur of the rows of ocean waves filled <s>Amīnā's</s> ear-cavities.

children.text: Atha yāvat parāvartate sā vātāyanāt tāvat pādacāradhvanim iva kasyāpy aśrauṣīt.
children.translated_text: Then, just as she was turning away from the window, she heard what sounded like someone's footsteps.

children.text: Dhvaninānenākṛṣṭeva gavākṣasavidhaṃ punaḥ sā yayau.
children.translated_text: As if drawn by that sound, she went to the window again.

children.text: Na cirāc ca samīpavartinaḥ saudhasyādhastalabhāgān nirgachantī Hamidasya śarīrākṛtiḥ punas tasyā dṛkpathe nyapatat.
children.translated_text: Before long, the bodily form of <s>Hāmid</s>, emerging from the lower portions of the adjacent mansion, fell again within her line of sight.

children.text: Himadhavalavasanopari śyāmakṣaumaprāvāro raktaturkoṣṇīṣaś ca niśākarakaranicaye vailakṣaṇyaṃ bhejāte.
children.translated_text: Over snow-white garments, a dark linen shawl and a red Turkish turban were conspicuous in the moon's rays.

children.text: Tataś ca gavākṣajālaprasāritai rajatamārjanīnibhaiḥ kalānidhikaranikaraiḥ saṃśodhitāndhakāre payodhiphenasaṃdoheneva nirmite śayanīya upaviśya saṃdehakoponmathitahṛdayā mukham adhaḥ kṛtvā niḥśvasyoṣṇaṃ ca sā tūṣṇīṃ tasthau.
children.translated_text: Then, on a bed made as if from ocean foam, illuminated by moonbeams like silver brooms spread through the window lattice that had dispelled the darkness, she sat down, her heart agitated by doubt and anger, bowed her head, sighed hotly, and remained silent.

children.text: Evaṃ catasṛṣu niśāsu naiśānveṣaṇam upākramatāmīnā yāvat sā Saralāyāḥ kapaṭasya saṃjātapratyayābhūt.
children.translated_text: Thus on four nights, <s>Amīnā</s> undertook this nocturnal investigation, until she became convinced of <s>Saralā's</s> deception.

children.text: Saralāhamidayor madhye nibhṛtāsaktisambandhaviṣaye na ko 'pi saṃdehaleśa iti niścitamatiḥ sā samabhūt.
children.translated_text: Regarding the matter of a secret romantic relationship between <s>Saralā</s> and <s>Hāmid</s>, she became firmly convinced that there was not the slightest room for doubt.

children.text: Pratinaktaṃ vyatikaram imaṃ pratyakṣīkṛtya lohitavadanā kopasphuradadharā jājvalyamānalocanā śayane kṛtapadā parśvadvaye muhurmuhur luṭhantī nairāśyād avātiṣṭhata.
children.translated_text: Having witnessed this transgression night after night, red-faced, her lips trembling with anger, her eyes blazing, she lay in bed tossing from side to side repeatedly, overcome by despair.

children.text: Kutarkaparavaśeyaṃ kriyāsamabhihāreṇodgacchadroṣabāṣpā krodhāgninā lulitalulitāṅgakais tāmyati sma pratidinam.
children.translated_text: Overwhelmed by false reasoning, with tears of anger rising from her actions' interpretation, tormented day after day with limbs writhing in the fire of wrath, she suffered.

children.text: Aho kathaṃ nādyāvadhi Saralāyā gūḍhakauṭilyaṃ na tarkitaṃ mandadhiyā mayeti muhurmuhur vicintayantī bhṛśam akupyad ātmane.
children.translated_text: 'Alas! How has the hidden deceitfulness of <s>Saralā</s> not been suspected until today by dull-witted me!' — thinking thus again and again, she became greatly angry at herself.

children.text: Atha pūrvavad yadā saha sakhyā śūcīśilpaṃ kartuṃ Saralā tasyāḥ prāsādaṃ samāyāt tadāmīnā'tyantanirutsāhā kopenāntareva tātapyamānā
hāsyavivarjitā samatiṣṭhata.
children.translated_text: remained devoid of laughter.
Then, as before, when <s>Saralā</s> came to her mansion to do needlework with her friend, <s>Amīnā</s>, utterly without enthusiasm, inwardly burning with anger

children.text: Kaiścid api gṛhakāryavyavasthākleśair udvejitā syat sahacarīti Saralā tām ullāsayituṃ savinodaṃ prāyatata.
children.translated_text: Thinking that her companion might be troubled by some difficulties of domestic management, <s>Saralā</s> tried to cheer her up with humor.

children.text: Param adhikādhikam audāsīnyam evāvalambya vimanāyamānā sthithavaty Amīnā.
children.translated_text: But <s>Amīnā</s> remained dispirited, clinging to ever-increasing indifference.

children.text: Uccaiḥ pustakapaṭhanaṃ cikīrṣuṃ Saralāṃ sapadi sapadi sahastavikṣepaṃ pratyākhyāt sā.
children.translated_text: She immediately rejected <s>Saralā</s>, who wished to read a book aloud, with a wave of her hand.

children.text: Prativāraṃ yadā Saralā viśrambhālāpaṃ kartuṃ prāvartata tadā tadvacobhir bhūyo vituṣṭahṛdayam ivātmānaṃ sā prādarśayat.
children.translated_text: Every time <s>Saralā</s> began to engage in intimate conversation, she displayed herself as if her heart were further displeased by those words.

children.text: Tadanu Saralā smāraṃ smāraṃ kaver uktim atiparicayād avajñā saṃtatagamanād
anādaro
children.translated_text: comes disregard'

children.text: bhavatīti vyaramad gamanāt sakhyā harmyam.
children.translated_text: — ceased going to her friend's mansion.
Then <s>Saralā</s>, repeatedly recalling the poet's saying — 'From excessive familiarity comes contempt; from constant visiting

children.text: Amīnāyā hṛdi tāvat sahacarīṃ prati vidveṣāgnir adhikādhikaṃ samudjvalat.
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, in <s>Amīnā</s>'s heart, the fire of hatred toward her companion blazed ever more intensely.

children.text: Anavarataṃ ca vyacintayat sā yadā bālyād yasyāṃ pūrṇaśo vyaśvasaṃ seyam adya katham īdṛgadharmakarmaṇi pravṛttābhūt tatrāpi nijasakhyāḥ saha vallabhena.
children.translated_text: And she constantly thought: 'She in whom I placed complete trust since childhood — how has she now engaged in such immoral conduct, and that too with her own friend's beloved?'

children.text: Madhuramadhuravacāṃsi matpuraḥ samudīrya parokṣaṃ mām kathaṃ sā pratāritavatī.
children.translated_text: 'Speaking the sweetest of sweet words before me, how has she deceived me behind my back!'

children.text: Ahaha! Kathaṃ kamalām iva vimalāṃ
śāradām iva viśāradāṃ
children.translated_text: as learned as <s>Śāradā</s>

children.text: satīm iva satīṃ svāṃ pradarṣayantī malinahṛdayā sthitavaty etāvat kālam.
children.translated_text: as faithful as a true <s>satī</s> — has she remained all this time with a soiled heart!'
'Alas! How, showing herself as pure as a lotus

children.text: Ahaṃ ca tāṃ viśvasanīyāṃ prāṇapriyāṃ ca bhaginīm iva samabhāvayam.
children.translated_text: 'And I regarded her as trustworthy, as dear as life, like a sister.'

children.text: Api Hāmidasya vaibhavena mohitā syāt sā yat svapateḥ patnīvatsalasya parokṣa vyabhicārakarmaṇi prāvartateyam.
children.translated_text: 'Could she have been beguiled by <s>Hāmid</s>'s wealth, that she has engaged in adulterous conduct behind the back of her husband, who is devoted to his wife?'

children.text: Kīdṛśo 'yaṃ viśvāsaghātaḥ.
children.translated_text: 'What a betrayal of trust this is!'

children.text: Kīdṛśīyaṃ cañcalatā cittasya
yan matsahacaryaiva viśveṣāṃ narmapātraṃ kṛtāsmi.
children.translated_text: that through my own companion I have been made an object of ridicule for all!'
'What fickleness of heart is this

children.text: Ahaha! Kathaṃ nāma tasyā viṣayāsaktiṃ vatsareṣv eteṣu nāvidam.
children.translated_text: 'Alas! How did I not discover her attachment to sensual pleasures in all these years!'

children.text: Kutaś ceyaṃ matgehasavidhe kṛtāvāsābhūta.
children.translated_text: 'And why did she take up residence near my house?'

children.text: Api bhartuḥ parokṣe nibhṛtadurācārāya vyavasitam itthaṃ tayā.
children.translated_text: 'Has she thus resolved upon secret misconduct behind her husband's back?'

children.text: Bāhyato mugdhānanāyā vinayasaṃpannāyāś ca tasyā hṛdi kauṭilyāhiḥ katham āśritaḥ syāt.
children.translated_text: 'How could the serpent of deceit dwell in the heart of one who is outwardly innocent-faced and endowed with modesty?'

children.text: Sarvā api sahacarya ātmānaṃ nirāgasaṃ pradarśayantyo 'viśvasanīyāḥ syuḥ.
children.translated_text: 'All female companions who present themselves as blameless must be untrustworthy.'

children.text: Itthaṃ tarkavitarkakaṇṭakanikaravyathitā sā Saralāṃ prastutaviṣayam uddiśya viśakalayya praṣṭukāmāpi svapratiṣṭhāyā alīkadarpāj joṣaṃ sthitavatī.
children.translated_text: Thus tormented by a thicket of conjectures and counter-conjectures, though she wished to confront <s>Saralā</s> and question her directly about the matter at hand, she remained silent out of false pride for her own reputation.

children.text: Saralāyāś cirasakhyaṃ tadīyamadhuravacaś ca svapna ivendrajālam iva māyādarśanam ivāmināyāḥ pratyabhād idānīm.
children.translated_text: <s>Saralā</s>'s long friendship and her sweet words now appeared to <s>Amīnā</s> like a dream, like a magic show, like an illusory vision.

children.text: Ādhiṃ cātmano rahasi sahamānāvātiṣṭhata sā.
children.translated_text: And she remained, bearing her anguish in solitude.

children.text: Atha gacchatsu varṣeṣu śiśur eko 'mīnāyāḥ kenāpi vyādhinā grasta ity
ākarṇya
children.translated_text: hearing this —

children.text: tasya śuśrūṣāyāṃ sakhyai sahāyyaṃ praditsuḥ Saralā sānunayaṃ patradvārā tasyai
children.translated_text: <s>Saralā</s>, wishing to offer help to her friend in nursing the child, through a letter with gentle entreaty

children.text: nyavedayat
children.translated_text: conveyed this to her
Then, as years passed, when one of <s>Amīnā</s>'s children was afflicted by some illness —

children.text: Paraṃ lekham imaṃ prāvaraṇād apasāryaiva yathāgataṃ vāhakāyād āpayad Amīnā.
children.translated_text: But <s>Amīnā</s>, merely removing the letter from its envelope, sent it back as it came through the messenger.

children.text: Anena paramodvignāpi Saralā sakhyai nādruhyan manāg api.
children.translated_text: Though greatly distressed by this, <s>Saralā</s> did not bear the slightest ill will toward her friend.

children.text: Rugṇārbhakasyāmīnāyāś ca vṛttaṃ svasevakamukhād upalabhya joṣaṃ sthitā.
children.translated_text: Learning of the condition of the sick child and of <s>Amīnā</s> through her own servants, she remained silent.

children.text: Athaikavatsarottaraṃ Hamido 'kasmāt kenāpi nirupāyarogeṇākrānto maraṇonmukhaḥ sthitaḥ.
children.translated_text: Then, after one more year, <s>Hāmid</s> was suddenly seized by some incurable disease and lay facing death.

children.text: Krameṇa sa ca naṣṭollāghatāśo nacirād vinaṣṭavāg āsanna
prāyo'ntakāla
children.translated_text: the end of his life

children.text: iti jñātvā Saralāyā gṛhasya diśam aṅgulyā nirdiśya muhurmuhuḥ kāpi
children.translated_text: — knowing this, pointing with his finger toward the direction of <s>Saralā</s>'s house, again and again

children.text: samāhūtayāmītīṅgitenaivāsūcayaj
children.translated_text: he indicated through gestures alone that 'she should be summoned'

children.text: joṣam.
children.translated_text: silently.
Gradually, having lost all hope of recovery and soon having lost his speech, being near

children.text: Bhartur āśayam avagatyāpi tasya parayoṣidāsaktim anabhinandamānā tatsūcanam avāmaṃstāmīnā.
children.translated_text: Though understanding her husband's wish, <s>Amīnā</s>, not approving his attachment to another woman, disregarded that indication.

children.text: Saralāyā ākṛtir hi hṛdi tasyāḥ śyāmaśyāmā mṛtyucchāyeva santatam
avasthitāsīt

For the image of <s>Saralā</s> in her heart was dark and gloomy, like the shadow of death, constantly

children.text: Atha pañcaṣadinottaraṃ bhagavato bhāskarasyāstamanasamaye Hamidaḥ prati paralokaṃ prasthitaḥ.
children.translated_text: Then, after five or six days, at the time of the setting of the blessed sun, <s>Hāmid</s> departed for the next world.

children.text: Tasya nidhanavṛttaṃ prativeśināṃ sapadi śrutipathe nyapatad acirāc ca
sarvato 'pi
children.translated_text: from all directions

children.text: nagare prāsarat.
children.translated_text: spread throughout the city.
The news of his death immediately fell upon the ears of the neighbors, and soon

children.text: Bhartur mṛtyunā śokākulābhūd Amīneti na
paraṃ tasyākasmikāntena stambhitā nijaśayanāgare niścalātiṣṭhat.
children.translated_text: rather, she stood motionless in her bedchamber, stunned by his sudden end.
It is not that <s>Amīnā</s> was overwhelmed with grief at her husband's death

children.text: Paricarāṇāṃ gamanāgamaninādena vṛddhasevakānām ākrośakallolena ca jāgaritā.
children.translated_text: She was awakened by the sounds of servants coming and going and by the waves of wailing of the old attendants.

children.text: Tasyā bālakāḥ saṃbhrāntāḥ saṃtrastāś cābhyadhāvan mātuḥ śayyālayam.
children.translated_text: Her children, bewildered and frightened, ran to their mother's bedchamber.

children.text: Sā ca bālavatsalā gāḍhaṃ tān pariṣvajya mṛdulavacobhiś ca samāsvāsya nijaparyaṅke śāyitavatī.
children.translated_text: And she, being affectionate toward her children, embraced them tightly, comforted them with gentle words, and laid them on her own bed.

children.text: Supteṣu teṣu Hamidasya sevako niḥśabdaṃ tām upetya nyavedayad yathāsnāpito dhūpito gandhādirūṣito vigrahaḥ svāminah.
children.translated_text: When they had fallen asleep, <s>Hāmid</s>'s servant approached her silently and informed her that the master's body had been bathed, fumigated, and anointed with perfumes and such.

children.text: Na cirād āyāsyanti nāgarikā anukampina
ito neṣyanty adhaḥ svāminaḥ pūtadeham uttaravidher anuṣṭhānārtham.
children.translated_text: and they will take the master's purified body down from here for the performance of the final rites.'
'Soon the compassionate townspeople will arrive

children.text: Purohitā hi samāyātāḥ.
children.translated_text: 'For the priests have already arrived.'

children.text: Ity uktayā śīghram āyāmi tāvad iti pratyuktas tayā paricārako 'pāsarat.
children.translated_text: Having been told thus, and she having replied 'I shall come quickly,' the servant departed.

children.text: Patyur antimadarśanasyecchayā 'mīnāntaḥpurān nirgatya dīrghadīrghagṛhābhyantaramārgān dīpamālābhir udbhāsitān samullaṅghya prāsādasya viśālasopānasamīpasthasya Hamidasya śayyāgṛhasya saṃnidhiṃ kathaṃ katham api prāpa.
children.translated_text: With the desire for a final glimpse of her husband, <s>Amīnā</s> emerged from the inner quarters, traversed the long interior corridors of the house illuminated by rows of lamps, and somehow reached the vicinity of <s>Hāmid</s>'s bedchamber near the great staircase of the mansion.

children.text: Atha yāvat prakoṣṭhasya dvāram udghāṭayitum sā pravartate tāvat paśyati sopānapaṅktim ārohantīṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ Saralām.
children.translated_text: Then, just as she was about to open the door of the chamber, she saw <s>Saralā</s> slowly ascending the flight of stairs.

children.text: Niśāmyaināṃ śītaśītasamīreṇa kampamānāṅgayaṣṭir iva tasthau vidhavā.
children.translated_text: Seeing her, the widow stood still, her body trembling as if shaken by a cold, cold breeze.

children.text: Avanatamukhī Saralā ca yāvat sahānubhūtiṃ pradarśayitum icchantī sakhīṃ saprema samāliṅgituṃ karapallavau vistārayati tāvad Amīnā tāṃ sahastavikṣepaṃ nivārya bravīti kaṭusvareṇa samāyātāsi niḥsaṃśayaṃ vallabhasyāntimadarśanāyeti.
children.translated_text: And as <s>Saralā</s>, with downcast face, wishing to show sympathy, extended her hands to embrace her friend lovingly, <s>Amīnā</s> pushed her away with a wave of her hand and spoke in a harsh voice: 'You have come, no doubt, for a final look at your beloved!'

children.text: Naivaṃ naivam.
children.translated_text: 'Not so, not so!'

children.text: Āyātāsmi khalu tvatkṛta iti paścāt pracalitā vikampitaśirāḥ pratyuvāca Saralā.
children.translated_text: 'I have come indeed for your sake,' replied <s>Saralā</s>, stepping back, her head trembling.

children.text: Apradattapratyuttarā ghanasaṃśayatamasāvṛtahṛdayā yāvad Amīnā bhartur āvāsadvāraṃ samudghāṭayati tāvad antaḥ kāñcana kāñcanāṅgīm aṅganāṃ dṛṣṭvā sākrośaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ pracalitā'mīnā.
children.translated_text: Without giving a reply, her heart shrouded in dense clouds of suspicion, when <s>Amīnā</s> opened the door to her husband's chamber, she saw inside a certain golden-limbed woman, and with a cry she staggered backward.

children.text: Kim idam? Keyam? Kuta iyam! Ahaha!
children.translated_text: 'What is this? Who is she? Where has she come from! Alas!'

children.text: ity udīrayantī khalitasvareṇa cakitā visphāritalocanā sthambiteva sā sthitā.
children.translated_text: — exclaiming thus in a faltering voice, startled, with wide-open eyes, she stood as if paralyzed.

children.text: Puṣpamālācchāditasya Hamidasya hi śayanasya savidhaṃ vinyastajānuḥ śyāmasūkṣmadukūlāmbaraveṣṭitāṅgayaṣṭiś cāruvadanā gauravarṇā śirīṣasukumāratanur mṛtasya pādayor nihitaśirāḥ śokajvālāvaliḍheva haridrākṣālitavadaneva niḥśabdaṃ vilapantī muktakaṇṭhaṃ kācit taruṇī vyaloki.
children.translated_text: For near <s>Hāmid</s>'s bed, which was covered with garlands of flowers, kneeling with her head placed at the feet of the dead man, a certain young woman was seen — her slender body wrapped in dark, fine silk garments, fair-complexioned, beautiful-faced, her body as delicate as a <s>śirīṣa</s> flower — weeping silently and then with full throat, as if consumed by flames of grief, her face appearing as though washed with turmeric.

children.text: Amīnayā sānuyogaṃ nirdiṣṭām enām ālokya Saralā karṇe 'japat:
children.translated_text: Seeing this woman whom <s>Amīnā</s> had pointed out accusingly, <s>Saralā</s> whispered in her ear:

children.text: Sakhi sahaja evāsyāḥ śokodvegajanito vilāpo vigatāsoḥ prāṇeśvarasya kṛte.
children.translated_text: 'Friend, this woman's lamentation, born of grief and agitation, is natural — it is for her departed lord.'

children.text: Tayor dīrghānurāgābhijñayā tvayā bhāvyam.
children.translated_text: 'You should understand the long-standing love between those two.'

children.text: Viditavṛttāḥ sarve 'pi prativeśino
'treti
children.translated_text: here.'
'All the neighbors too know the story

children.text: Katham? Kadā? Tvam evāsya praṇeśvarīti
mayākalitam iti
children.translated_text: '— so I had assumed' —

children.text: prālapad Amīnā'sphuṭam.
children.translated_text: murmured <s>Amīnā</s> indistinctly.
'How? When? I thought you alone were his beloved!'

children.text: Vismitā stambhiteva vacanam Amīnāyā nāvagacchantīva kṣaṇaṃ visphāritanayanāvātiṣṭhata Saralā.
children.translated_text: Astonished, as if stunned, as if not comprehending <s>Amīnā</s>'s words, <s>Saralā</s> stood for a moment with wide-open eyes.

children.text: Tataś ca vivarṇavadanam Amīnāyā vilokya sā savegam abhāṇīt.
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Amīnā</s>'s pale face, she spoke with urgency:

children.text: Ayi mūḍhamate! Yathaihikasampattivaibhavaiśvaryādibhiḥ sanāthīkṛtāsi tvaṃ vidhinā
tathaiva tena patyuḥ premodrekasampattyaikasukhabhākkṛto 'sti jano 'yam.
children.translated_text: so too has this person been made the sole recipient of the happiness of her husband's overflowing love.'
'O foolish one! Just as you have been blessed by fate with worldly wealth, prosperity, and sovereignty

children.text: Prāṇeśvaram antareṇetarapuruṣā me bhrātṛsamānā eva.
children.translated_text: 'Apart from my beloved husband, all other men are to me like brothers.'

children.text: Iti samudīrya viratavacanā
ste Saralā tāvad Amīnā lajjayā natamukhī niḥśabdā sthitavatī.
children.translated_text: <s>Saralā</s> stood, while <s>Amīnā</s> remained with her face bowed in shame, speechless.
Having spoken thus and fallen silent

children.text: Muhūrtottaraṃ labdhaprakṛtir uvāca Saralā punaḥ.
children.translated_text: After a moment, having regained her composure, <s>Saralā</s> spoke again:

children.text: Avagatam idānīṃ mayā tava māṃ prati durāgrahahalāhalavikārasya kāraṇam.
children.translated_text: 'I have now understood the cause of the poisonous transformation of your obstinate prejudice toward me.'

children.text: Bālasakhyām anindyāyāṃ kutarkajanitaduṣṭasaṃśayapiśācabhāram āropya pañcasu varṣeṣv eteṣu tāṃ hanta dṛkpathād akāraṇaṃ niṣkāsya durmanāyamānam ātmānaṃ paryatāpayas tvaṃ vṛthā.
children.translated_text: Having placed upon your blameless childhood friend the burden of the demon of wicked doubt born from false reasoning, for these five years you, alas, drove her from your sight without cause, and tormented yourself, brooding in vain.

children.text: Vākpratiṣṭhāni dehināṃ vyavahāratantrāṇi.
children.translated_text: The dealings of embodied beings are founded upon speech.

children.text: Vāci khalu satyāsatyahetavo vyavasthitāḥ.
children.translated_text: Indeed, the grounds of truth and falsehood reside in speech.

children.text: Yadi saralavacanena mām aprakṣyas tvaṃ tarhi yāthārthyam avediṣyaḥ.
children.translated_text: If you had asked me with straightforward words, you would have known the truth.

children.text: Paraṃ hṛdi nibhṛtaṃ vaimanasyam āśritya vṛthā saṃśayajanitābhidrohāgnisantaptā mṛgīva ghorasaṃdehajanitakopavyāghrā
ghrātā nibhṛtam aśrupravāhair vṛthā snātā kriyāsamabhihāreṇa māṃ hṛdi śapantī ca dīrghakālaṃ sthitāsi.
children.translated_text: secretly weeping, bathed in vain with streams of tears, cursing me in your heart through the performance of rituals, you remained thus for a long time.
But harboring hidden displeasure in your heart, scorched in vain by the fire of enmity born of doubt, like a doe stalked by a tiger of terrible suspicion-born anger

children.text: Kāmaṃ tava bhartuś ceṣṭitaṃ nocitam āsīt khalu.
children.translated_text: Certainly your husband's conduct was not proper, indeed.

children.text: Paraṃ yavanadharmeṇa svadāretarāyāḥ parakīyāyāḥ aṅgīkāro yathānyāyam iti pratipadyata ity api viditam āsīt te.
children.translated_text: But it was also known to you that, according to the custom of the <s>Yavanas</s> (Muslims/foreigners), the acceptance of another woman, one other than one's own wife, is considered lawful.

children.text: Ākarṇyaitan nipatyāmīnā Saralāyāḥ pādayor viśithilavacanavinyāsā'timandasvarā lajjayā
nana āvirbhūtavividhabhāvabhaṅgā baddhāñjalir abravīt.
children.translated_text: with various emotional expressions manifesting, she joined her palms and spoke.
Hearing this, <s>Amīnā</s> fell at <s>Saralā's</s> feet like a fish, with faltering arrangement of words, in an extremely soft voice, with shame

children.text: Sakhi! Kṣamyatāṃ
kṣamyatāṃ jano 'yam.
children.translated_text: may this person be forgiven.
Friend! May I be forgiven

children.text: Sanāthāpy ahaṃ cirāt parāṅmukhībhūte nāthe 'nāthībhūteva kathaṃ kathamapi kālam ayāpayam.
children.translated_text: Though I had a lord, when my lord turned his face away for so long, I somehow managed to pass the time as though I were lordless.

children.text: Nāthasya nidhanenādya yathāpūrvaṃ nirviśeṣam avasthitāsmi khalu.
children.translated_text: With the death of my lord, today I remain just as before, without any distinction.

children.text: Paraṃ cirād ātmanaiva niḥsāritabālasakhī daivayogāt punar mayopalabdheti madbhāgyabhāskaro 'yam iti pramuditāntaraṅgāsmīti vacaḥ punaruktir eva syāt.
children.translated_text: But that a childhood friend long cast out by myself has by the chance of fate been found again by me — this is the sun of my fortune — that I am overjoyed within, to say this would indeed be mere repetition.

children.text: Hanta! Itaḥ param ājīvam āvām ubhe dṛḍhabaddhasakhye sthāsyāva
children.translated_text: Alas! Henceforth, for life, we two shall remain firmly bound in friendship

children.text: ity udīrya Saralāṃ gāḍham āśliṣya nijaśayanāgāram enām anayad Amīnā.
children.translated_text: — saying this, embracing <s>Saralā</s> tightly, <s>Amīnā</s> led her to her own bedchamber.
